description: LexFlow default capabilities — Maximum security, zero network access
_audit_BE-5: Capability scope hardening (audit-report.md HIGH F3 / BE-5). Each shell:allow-execute entry is scoped to a specific qpdf or typst invocation pattern actually used by src-tauri/src/doc_tools.rs. Validators reject leading '-' in path slots so file paths cannot be smuggled as flags. Backend already canonicalises paths (validate_input_path / validate_output_path), but defense-in-depth requires capability-level enforcement. DO NOT widen these without security review.
_audit_path_validator: Path slots use ^[A-Za-z0-9/._\-:\\ ]{1,4096}$ — alphanumerics, '/', '.', '_', '-', ':', '\\', space. Length cap 4096. Rejects newlines, control chars, shell metacharacters ($, ;, |, &, `, *, ?, !, <, >, etc.) and any leading dash.
_audit_pagespec_validator: Page-spec slots use ^[0-9,zr\-]{1,1024}$ — digits, comma, 'z' (last-page sentinel), 'r' (reverse), '-' (range). Used for qpdf --pages and --rotate ranges.

permissions._audit_purpose: Sidecar invocations: typst (PDF generation from .typ source) + qpdf (PDF transforms). NO other binaries permitted. NO arbitrary shell commands.

allow._audit_mode: typst compile <input.typ> <output.pdf> --font-path <dir>  — used by images_to_pdf and any template that needs Libertinus Serif
allow.name: binaries/typst

allow._audit_mode: typst compile <input.typ> <output.pdf>  — used by add_watermark, add_page_numbers, redact_pdf (no font-path needed)
allow.name: binaries/typst

allow._audit_mode: qpdf --show-npages <input>  — used by pdf_info, add_watermark, add_page_numbers, redact_pdf for page count
allow.name: binaries/qpdf

allow._audit_mode: qpdf --show-encryption <input>  — reserved for future use; harmless read-only inspection
allow.name: binaries/qpdf

allow._audit_mode: qpdf --empty --pages <input> <pagespec> -- -- <output>  — used by remove_pages, extract_pages (split/keep specific pages)
allow.name: binaries/qpdf

allow._audit_mode: qpdf <input> --rotate=+<deg>:<pagespec> -- <output>  — used by rotate_pdf. The combined --rotate=+N:spec arg is matched as a single token; validator allows only digits, ':', ',', '-', '+', 'z', 'r' after the literal --rotate= prefix.
allow.name: binaries/qpdf

allow._audit_mode: qpdf <input> --overlay <overlay.pdf> -- -- <output>  — used by add_watermark, add_page_numbers, redact_pdf (overlay step). Note the literal '-- --' separator (qpdf overlay delimiter then qpdf positional delimiter).
allow.name: binaries/qpdf

allow._audit_mode: qpdf --decrypt <input> -- <output>  — used by unsecure_pdf when no password is supplied
allow.name: binaries/qpdf

allow._audit_TODO_BE-5_encrypt: TODO: enumerate qpdf --encrypt invocations (used by secure_pdf and redact_pdf step 5). The --encrypt syntax embeds a variable-length owner password (LF_<16hex> or user-supplied) and N flags whose count varies (--extract, --print, --modify, --assemble, --annotate, --form, --extract+--print+--modify only for redact). Backend already generates the owner password server-side from rand::random and validates paths. Until per-pattern entries are added, fall back to args:true scoped to qpdf only.
allow._audit_TODO_BE-5_decrypt_pwd: TODO: enumerate qpdf --password <pwd> --decrypt <input> -- <output>. Password is user-supplied — needs a length-bounded validator that does NOT leak via shell. See BE-4 (password-file fix) which may obviate this entry.
allow.name: binaries/qpdf
